item.title: The Most Expensive Chase Cards in Disney Lorcana Packs RIGHT NOW!
item.description:
Disney Lorcana|collecting|finance

The Most Expensive Chase Cards in Disney Lorcana Packs RIGHT NOW!

Wanna crack some Disney Lorcana? Scott's got your guide to all the biggest pulls, from $3,000 iconics to base legendaries

By Scott Mines

|@HowlingMines
|

Published Nov 10, 2026

|

13 min read

Copy Link
TCGplayer Series:

"I'm too shiny! Watch me dazzle like a diamond in the rough. Strut my stuff, my stuff is so shiny..."

I could embrace my inner Tamatoa all day, but that's not why you're here, is it?

I'm a self-admitted magpie when it comes to trading card games. There's just something about that dash of sparkle that makes my heart flutter. Unfortunately for my wallet, that does tend to encourage some frivolous spending on booster packs. I mean come on. It could be anything in there — it could even be that card I want!

If you're similarly cursed, it pays to be informed about the biggest hits inside each pack. If you're snapping up a great deal on a booster box, it's obvious that an Enchanted card is going to cover the cost of your purchase, but sometimes a smattering of foils and legendries is where the bread-and-butter value is secretly hidden. With each new booster set, there's more permutations of collectibles to consider than ever before. What exactly are you supposed to buy if you're looking for the best value for your money?

First, we've got to clarify some rules:

  • We're only going to be discussing cards found in big retail releases. That means no event promos, no Disney cruise exclusives and no wacky or wild misprints
  • I'll be using the ungraded market price as my guideline for inclusion in this article
  • Grading cards costs some serious money, so it's unfair to compare the all-time high of a PSA 10 to a raw card you just opened in your living room

All clear? Sweet. With the formalities out of the way, let's take a closer look at the most expensive cards you can find inside Disney Lorcana booster packs right now!

Hyperia City

The much-beloved Coco graced our game with the introduction of Hyperia City: a town infused with musical flair, modern living and fantastical heroes. Glimmers are hitting the streets to enjoy the nightlife and letting their creative sides cut loose... all while something more sinister works away in the back alleys and waterways.  

Hyperia City is cooling much faster than the handful of sets before it, as players and collectors alike struggle to solve which cards truly sit as grails and must-haves. I expect this set to remain volatile as the format evolves, which will make for some high-risk-high-reward investments if you're so inclined.  

I'll gladly admit that I lost the bet on this one. I thought that the untouchable iconography of a princess like Cinderella - Unintentional Icon would be untouchable in the world of chase cards, but Mickey Mouse - Best in Town is putting her to shame. The mouse with the most is one of the best cards in all of Disney Lorcana right now and is arguably more famous than his blonde counterpart.

The princesses are coming out in force in the Enchanted slot, though. The artwork on Ariel - Collector of Oddities is something else, which has transformed the card from something pretty to a must-have for Disney fans that don't normally engage with Disney Lorcana. Belle - Exceptional Writer isn't too far behind, while Aurora - Delightful Musician and Rapunzel - Outgoing Artist also sit comfortably around the $150 mark. I think the latter two are a steal at that price to be honest.  

Max Goof - Karaoke Star is the non-princess standout. The card is kicking butt in the Core Constructed format right now and certainly reads like a long-term powerhouse. If you're expecting to be drawing cards and questing for four for the rest of the year, it's a great pickup.  

Sadly, the epic rares are quite underwhelming this time around. The top three are holding their own purely off the back of Core Constructed playability, with Flash - Efficient Clerk and Toulouse - Rough and Tumble likely to see healthy amounts of play throughout their tenure in Core. Judy Hopps - Always Vigilant is one of the lynchpins of the Amber Sapphire Detectives deck and will remain popular for as long as it does.  

It's a similar story for the base variants of legendary cards, which continue to be worth less with each passing set. Only Max Goof - Karaoke Star sits above $5, with Shere Khan - Khan Industries CEO and Mulan - Martial Arts Master coming in second and third respectively.  

Personally, it's a big red flag when these cards aren't covering the cost of a pack anymore, but I can't pretend it isn't perfect for players who need to snap them up to play with.  

Attack of the Vine!

The second barrage of Pixar power came courtesy of Attack of the Vine!, which introduced much-beloved franchises like Monsters Inc, Up and Turning Red into the game's portfolio. It also spun up a fresh new rotation for Core Constructed, which had numerous new archetypes emerging and several older stalwarts depreciating as it made its grand entrance. 

Attack of the Vine! is very much riding a wave of success from the boom of popularity that Wilds Unknown created, leading to some wildly valuable iconic and enchanted cards. However, the sheer amount of packs opened has helped to bring most base rarity cards within anybody's budget. 

Lilo & Stitch - Fun-Loving Friends and Belle & Beast - Certain as the Sun are amongst the most valuable cards in Disney Lorcana history, with the latter pulling almost $2000 a copy at time of writing. I expect both of these cards to continue to blossom as Attack of the Vine! ages on account of their beautiful panoramic artworks. The colors are vibrant and they look super classy. 

This set also saw the introduction of tag-team cards, which would prove to create some of the most coveted enchanted cards on the market today. Winnie the Pooh & Piglet - Hunny Mages is a beast unto itself, slowly rivalling the previous hunny wizard for the highest price tag on an enchanted. Woody & Buzz Lightyear - Best Buddies and Minnie Mouse & Mickey Mouse - Adventuring Duo may be slightly adrift of the hunny duo, but they're still comfortably commanding hundreds of dollars each. 

There's really only one epic holding its own and commanding a premium. Winnie the Pooh - Hunny Archmage is yet another beneficiary of the ever-growing Hunny Dynasty. Needless to say at this point, but if a future set contains more support for Pooh and friends, you should be pretty bullish on getting your hands on it. 

Meilin Lee - Losing Control and Boo - In Disguise also command between a couple dollars per copy if you're looking for other epics that may have constructed implications somewhere down the line. 

The drop-off on legendary cards in Attack of the Vine! is startling though. Mushu - Stealthy Dragon is the only card worth more than half a pack right now. This has some pros and cons: it's a fantastic boon if you're looking to sweep up singles for your deck, but it's a little frustrating if you prefer cracking boxes. That's the side effect of such expensive high-rarity cards — people open a ton of boxes and the price of lower rarity cards takes the hit. 

I do think Christopher Robin - Hunny Sage is a phenomenal buy at under $1. The card makes the Hunny deck tick and I'm expecting that deck to get additional support down the pipeline given the popularity of its characters.

Wilds Unknown

Pixar's debut in Disney Lorcana absolutely rocked the world of our little card game. Fan-favorite characters from Toy Story, The Incredibles and Brave stole the spotlight as the Infinity format began to blossom on the competitive stage, while simultaneously introducing Toy-themed decks into Core Constructed. 

I expect Wilds Unknown to age like a fine wine as additional synergy pieces for its archetypes come to life, but that doesn't mean it doesn't already feature some all-stars. After all, this was the set that caused the second resurgence of Disney Lorcana amongst collectors when it finally hit shelves. 

Buzz Lightyear - Jungle Ranger has gone to infinity and beyond. It's unquestionably the most coveted card from the set, with recorded sales of over $5,700 a copy. Merida - Formidable Archer is no slouch either, completing a commanding pair of iconic rares that will make this set a must-open product for years to come. 

It's no big surprise that the Toy Story Enchanted cards are boasting the highest price point either. Alien - True Believer looks phenomenal in person and features in almost every emerald toy deck, turning the little green men into a hot commodity. You've Got a Friend in Me is a similar story. An absolute banger known worldwide that'll appear in every amber toy deck for the rest of time? I don't mind if I do. 

Jesse - Lively Cowgirl might be the most surprising winner amongst these, but the card has proven to be a mainstay across Emerald Amber and Ruby Amber toy variant. I'm not shocked to see her performing so strong. 

The narrative for Toy Story continues through the epic cards, with Buzz Lightyear - Space Ranger, Woody - Waiting for a Friend, and Rex - Protective Dinosaur far and away the most valuable. 

In the legendary department, foil variants of Snow White - Merry as the Morning and Dale - Ready for His Shot are the biggest winners. The Snow White's part of a wider panorama with the remaining Seven Dwarf foils, which cannot be completed without her; while Dale has proven to be one of, if not the most competitive Legendary from the set, commanding a premium as a foil. It's showing up across both Core Constructed and Infinity, and I only expect it to get better as more products release. 

Winterspell

The frosty first foray into 2026 ticked nearly all of the boxes you'd want to see from a set so close to rotation. Winterspell introduced several archetype defining cards like Akood et Emuti and Grandmother Willow - Ancient Advisor into the game alongside a variety of winter-themed friends from across numerous franchises. It also say the Boost keyword iterated upon to become an evergreen part of the game. Big wins all around. 

At this stage, you should be expecting both iconic rares to be the biggest hits in the set. Moana - Curious Explorer and Pocahontas - Peacekeeper should both be seen as absolute slam dunks if you manage to find them inside your booster packs, with both cards seeing continuous growth in price since their release. 

Winterspell contains some of the more coveted enchanted cards in recent memory. Elsa - Ice Artisan continues the trend of the Frozen princess's domination with her higher rarity cards, while Eeyore - In the Way was a surprising winner to me, but it's hard to deny that the artwork is incredibly cute. The character has no other high rarity card in Disney Lorcana, which has led to fans of Winnie the Pooh snapping it up. 

The competitive players lent towards Angel - Experiment 624 as their preferred enchanted. Angel has been carving a legacy in numerous steel decks and should remain a mainstay of Core Constructed for the entirety of its time in the format, making for the perfect investment for invested players. 

Angel is also the biggest winner for base level legendaries for much the same reason, but I'm most impressed by a couple of the epic cards in this set. Typically, this rarity has fallen a little flat in terms of value, but Stitch - Carefree Snowboarder and Grandmother Willow - Ancient Advisor both consistently hold between $15-$20 a copy and see consistent play in multiple formats. I expect these to age very well. 

Whispers in the Well

We closed the page on 2025 with Disney Lorcana's tenth booster set, Whispers in the Well. The set had a somewhat unfair level of expectation placed on its shoulders as the first real injection of new cards since the rotation of Core Constructed. Would it land? Well, that's a mystery. The mystery was the entire point! 

Mickey and Minnie left a huge shadow for Hades - Looking for a Deal and Ariel - Ethereal Voice to escape from, and while they haven't reached the lofty heights of the iconic duo, they're clearly highly coveted collectibles. Hades has proven to be very playable at the tournament tables, while Ariel stands tall as one of Disney's most beloved princesses.

The playability bump has also bolstered the price of some of the top enchanted cards in Whispers in the Well. Demona - Scourge of the Wyvern Clan has cemented herself as a cornerstone for Amethyst decks across the format, while Goliath - Clan Leader makes constant appearances in steel decks willing to dump their hand. Cinderella - Dream Come True had people crying out for bans before she was released! That's how darn good this card is! And currently they're all topped by the blinding demand for enchanted Spooky Sight, a surprising crossover card between two very different Disney properties.

All four of these cards seem steadfast enough to see play for many months to come, encouraging players and collectors alike to invest in their highest possible rarities. That's great news for you if you find one inside your packs. 

Epics from this set are underperforming across the board, with Elsa - Exploring the Unknown standing as the only one holding firm above $10. In the Legendary department, the same names find themselves appearing at the top of the list: Demona, Cinderella and Hades. The Headless Horseman - Terror of Sleepy Hollow is another big pull, too. These are the cards you're really hoping to find in your average pack of Whispers in the Well. 

Fabled

The dawn of the second chapter of Disney Lorcana. Fabled released to a surprising amount of fanfare in September 2025. The game's ninth set triggered the first rotation of Core Constructed and flipped expectations for the future firmly on their head. Fabled is stuffed with a bevy of reprints, new rarities to chase and illustrious enchanted rares for all-time favorite cards.

The iconic rares for Mickey Mouse - Brave Little Prince and Minnie Mouse - Sweetheart Princess are the headliners. These are the first Iconic rares to make it to print and carry uniquely foiled accents and an aura of their own. They're beautiful must-have cards for any high-level collector and sport the price tag to match. A copy of Mickey Mouse - Brave Little Prince will set you back over $3500, while Minnie sits comfortably at $3000 and rising.

In the Enchanted department, Winnie the Pooh - Hunny Wizard, Ariel - Adventurous Collector, and I2I steal the show. None of these cards are played much in tournaments, but all three connect to Disney fandom in unique ways and with Fabled becoming so tough to find, their prices have risen dramatically (especially Pooh, who has gained somewhat of a cult following).

Other Enchanteds like Dumbo - Ninth Wonder of the Universe, Mickey Mouse - Steamboat Pilot, and Circle of Life are all huge pulls as well. Fabled is just loaded with massive hits.

Fabled Epics have aged well too, after being long undervalued: Aurora - Holding Court, Mickey Mouse - Standard Bearer, and Elsa - Snow Queen are all well over $30 in Market Price, and may very well be higher by the time you read this. Aurora's proven to be a favorite amongst Disney collectors and shines in Amber Steel aggressive shells, while Elsa is exploding in popularity as Frozen 3 approaches. 

 

Dumbo used to rule the roost amongst Legendary cards, but now there are several legendaries that carry a $40+ price tag. Max Goof - Chart Topper and Circle of Life stand out as cards worth adding to your collection in addition to the elephant in the room as they continue to dominate the Core Constructed format.

item.title: Dragapult ex/Crushing Hammer Deck Guide (Pokémon TCG)
item.description:
Pokémon|competitive

Dragapult ex/Crushing Hammer Deck Guide (Pokémon TCG)

Crush your opponent's dreams with a coin flip.

By Natalie Millar

|@nataliem9999
|

Published Nov 11, 2026

|

5 min read

Copy Link
TCGplayer Series: Pokémon Deck Guides

Hello everyone! Dragapult ex with Crushing Hammer is currently the undisputed best deck in the format, and that's looking to remain true in the Delta Reign format. The 60 cards below have already won two Regional Championships and I wouldn't be surprised if it won another major tournament prior to rotation!

Dragapult ex/Crushing Hammer Deck List

This deck looks very simple but it has a wide variety of game plans. The core of the deck is the Dragapult line; Drakloak's Recon Directive ability filters through your deck and Dragapult's Phantom Dive is one of the most powerful attacks in the format, setting up spread damage and multiple knockouts. The cards in the Dragapult deck are so efficient that you have a ton of deck space to play many luxury cards, which has resulted in the default version of Dragapult ex playing four copies of Crushing Hammer. Crushing Hammer looks a little strange when it's a flip card, but many decks in the current format rely heavily on their attachments for turn and hitting an early Crushing Hammer heads will reliably buy you a whole turn against the aggressive decks. Crushing Hammer also allows you to have an alternate win condition of resource denial and to sometimes act as a control deck. This deck is one of the best users of Budew's Itchy Pollen, which prevents Items and slows down the opponent in the early game.

Because of the Fire and Psychic cost of Phantom Dive, you're incentivized to play Energy acceleration Supporter cards like Crispin and Rosa's Encouragement in this deck. This gives you the extra attachments to take advantage of Munkidori's Adrena-Brain, which is arguably the strongest card in the format. There are several scary Stadium cards in the format like Battle Cage, Legendary Pyroduct and Nighttime Mine, but your counter Stadium Risky Ruins also doubles as your win condition since it damages your Pokémon when they come into play, enabling you to move the damage over with Munkidori. This deck also has the room for a 1/1 line of Dudunsparce with Run Away Draw, which both is extra draw power and is a way to win in stalled game states since you can continuously loop a Pokémon coming into play to add an extra 20 damage to your opponents board.

The rest of the cards in this deck all have the goal of enabling your game plan. Three Night Stretchers recover Pokémon and Energy to rebuild your setup against early knockouts, Meowth ex and Fezandipiti ex get you out of mediocre hands, and you have the 11 Pokémon Search Items to set up your board.

One of the most underrated aspects of this deck is the flexibility of attackers. There are many scenarios across different matchups where you can attack with Munkidori's Mind Bend or Fezandipiti's Cruel Arrow, and some matchups where Cruel Arrow is your primary game plan to avoid losing to Lillie's Clefairy ex's Fairy Zone ability. Boss's Orders is both used as aggression but also as an Energy denial card, as you can sometimes Boss up an opposing Meowth ex to deny your opponents next attachment, acting as an additional Crushing Hammer heads.

This deck is also one of the best users of Unfair Stamp in the current format. You primarily play with a single-Prize board in the early game, and the opponent KOing Budew often results in them getting Unfair Stamped. This deck combines multiple pieces of disruption together with Crushing Hammer, Unfair Stamp and Boss's Orders alongside Phantom Dive on something like a Fezandipiti or Latias ex without taking a KO, forcing the opponent to find multiple cards to KO the Dragapult without the assistance of Flip the Script. If your opponent just hits the Dragapult without taking the knockout, you often win the game immediately thanks to having so much damage to move over to their side with Munkidori. Judge also functions as another disruption card for this deck. While Judge is not as good as Special Red Card in the aggressive matchups, it's often for breaking stalemates where both players are building cards in hand and you want to initiate without fear of retaliation from a potential Unfair Stamp and Crushing Hammers. There are several lists of this deck that also have Special Red Card alongside Unfair Stamp and Judge, but I don't think that Special Red Card is currently necessary.

The only real card slot is flexible in this deck is the third copy of Darkness Energy. There are many options to play in this slot, including Dudunsparce ex to answer Big Basic decks, Special Red Card as extra disruption, Jamming Tower as an extra Stadium bump and Psychic Energy to use Mind Bend more often. However, I like Darkness Energy since it's slightly better in the Dragapult mirror match, which is very important in the current format. Having more Munkidori than your opponent in that matchup is very important to control the damage in play and you can often win from multiple Prize cards down by having more access to Adrena-Brain throughout the game.

Dragapult ex is very popular right now, which has resulted in many of the other decks warping their strategy around countering it. Even though its internal game plan is so flexible, many of the decks you play against will feel like difficult matchups but even the seemingly difficult matchups like Basic Box, Hide & Sneak and Crustle are all very doable with the right game plan. When playing this deck, it's very important to be open minded about your decisions. Just because you're able to use Phantom Dive doesn't mean that it's correct to do so, and just because you're able to play Unfair Stamp doesn't mean that it's the best turn for it. You ideally want to play Unfair Stamp on a turn where you force your opponent to draw multiple cards for their ideal turn. Playing Unfair Stamp in the early game just to use Itchy Pollen is usually very weak as your opponent has multiple turns to draw out of the two cards, and this often turns into five cards by the time they need to play any cards to KO a potential Dragapult ex.

Despite Dragapult's reputation as not being fun to play against, it has produced some of the most interesting and dynamic games I've played in the current format. Regardless of which side is using Phantom Dive, the game will usually be interesting and have a ton of decisions to it, and I'm excited to see where this deck goes for the rest of its longevity in the Standard format!

item.title: What Decks Got The Biggest Upgrades From Stardust Trails?
item.description:
Gundam Card Game|competitive

What Decks Got The Biggest Upgrades From Stardust Trails?

Orb has a new Level 7, and how about that blocker Altron?

By Wren Melburn

|

Published Nov 13, 2026

|

3 min read

Copy Link
TCGplayer Series:

With all of Stardust Trails revealed and available in stores now, it's time to take a comprehensive look to see which decks picked up the most support! There are more unique tags and factions than ever before, and it's almost impossible for Bandai to not pick winners and losers long before players open their packs.

There are some clear winners and a few duds right out of the gate. I've been chasing the new Orb high end Blue/White blocker strategy with the new Infinite Justice. I've got to say during the release season I and many others figured the new Orb shell would be oppressive, and it lived up to those expectations.

Blue / White Orb

Unsurprisingly, the Infinite Justice is the perfect machine to slot right into the Orb/blocker archetype that's seeing play everywhere. 

  • 4 M1 Astray Shrike
  • 4 Waldfeld's Murasame
  • 3 Dom Trooper
  • 4 Murasame
  • 4 Akatsuki (Oowashi)
  • 2 Justice Gundam
  • 2 Infinite Justice Gundam
  • 4 Strike Freedom Gundam
  • 4 Andrew Waldfeld
  • 4 Kira Yamato
  • 3 Athrun Zala
  • 4 Overflowing Affection
  • 1 A Show of Resolve
  • 3 Archangel

Buy this deck on TCGplayer

The deck is diving deeper into its original gameplan thanks to the new cards. The Freedom deck uses blockers to stall for time until it can throw down the Strike Freedom at Level 8. Historically the deck had a vulnerable moment in the Level 5-7 area, where decks like MF could try to end the game before the Strike Freedom hit the board.

Now the Infinite Justice plugs that hole, ultimately widening the gap that SF has over its competition. The Infinite Justice drops down and pops an enemy unit back to hand, throwing off their tempo while you toss Athrun in the cockpit to really tear things up. Between popping something back into hand with the mobile suit and Athrun acting like he's a Guntank, you'll be able to get to your top end much safer. If your opponent doesn't answer the healthy refueling, tempo breaking Infinite Justice, the game is just over. 

Green / White G Team

Following up on how Orb got new toys, the G Team is finally back in full swing with Stardust Trails debuting new Eternal Waltz cards. The Altron, Heavyarms, and Sandrock are all really cool additions to the Wing Zero Green/White deck that's been around since the dawn of the game. 

  • 4 Gundam Heavyarms Custom (EW)
  • 4 Gundam Lfrith
  • 4 Altron Gundam (EW)
  • 3 Gundam Heavyarms Custom (EW)
  • 4 Gundam Sandrock Custom (EW)
  • 3 Gundam Sandrock Custom (EW)
  • 2 Shenlong Gundam
  • 4 Wing Gundam
  • 2 Wing Gundam Zero (EW)
  • 3 Wing Gundam Zero
  • 2 Chang Wufei
  • 4 Heero Yuy
  • 4 Quatre Raberba Winner
  • 4 Overflowing Affection
  • 3 Peacemillion

Buy this deck on TCGplayer

The big stand out card that really brings the Wing shell back to where it should be, is the new Altron Gundam. That nasty customer truly shakes up how the game plays out. With this version of the Altron being a Level 3, 3 Cost, it really messes with how most people are expecting things to go. The fact that it supes itself up the moment your opponent has a Level 5 in play, just means that you're never up against anything that you aren't prepared for. 

The rest of the deck shines really well with the original kit and the new EW Mobile Suits, so it's no big surprise I've seen this deck pull off some nasty stuff, and I can't wait to see it do more in the coming event season!

With this being the first few weeks of the play season it's really hard to get a bead on other decks, at least until we see more tournaments and how people break the newest toys. If I was a betting person, I wouldn't be surprised to see a Purple/Blue Alphacide list hit the top tables. I know it's one I've been looking forward to playing. But hey, you'll have to see what works best for you at the local level, and then bring your A game to the big leagues. Whatever you end up on, I'll see you out there on these Stardust Trails my fellow Pilots!

item.title: Top 10 Best-Selling MTG Cards of the Week - 11/13/2026
item.description:
Magic: The Gathering|collecting|finance

Top 10 Best-Selling MTG Cards of the Week - 11/13/2026

Pauper's on top.

By Jason Coles

|

Published Nov 13, 2026

|

4 min read

Copy Link
TCGplayer Series: Bestselling Cards of the Week

Did you know that the holiday shopping season is basically here? You're not behind on your shopping, are you? Truthfully this has nothing to do with this week's list of the best-selling Magic: The Gathering cards, but I wanted to bring it up as a helpful reminder. Anyway, Star Trek releases in full today, and brings with it an odd mix of actor's faces and some of the coolest mechanics you've ever seen in your life. Has that impacted the best-sellers?

Top 10 Best-Selling Magic: The Gathering Cards of the Week - 11/13/2026

To the surprise of nobody, Star Trek is taking over this list. There's no living long or prospering for other sets, it's almost entirely the final frontier outside of two cards. There are some surprise cards on the list from the set though, alongside some cards which are sure to be Commander staples for a long time to come as well. 

#10 Sphinx's Approach

Sphinx's Approach was last week's top entry, but has fallen flat compared to the appeal of Riker's beard. This three-mana blue instant lets you draw two cards, which is already good, then exile four copies of it from your graveyard to fetch up a sphinx from your library and put it into play. You can have as many copies of this card in a deck as you want too. 

#9 Brazen Bluff

Brazen Bluff is our first Star Trek card, and it's a really fun one. This two-mana red instant lets you choose a noncreature spell someone else casts. They can then either exile it, effectively making this a counterspell, or let you cast a noncreature spell of your own from your hand without paying its mana cost. It has a lot of layers in terms of meta play, and I'm looking forward to messing around with it. 

#8 Steam Vents & Blood Crypt

Steam Vents and Blood Crypt both sold very well this week. It's not a shock (pun intended). The shocklands have always been high-demand cards, and with the release of Star Trek they're all a lot more affordable than they've been in a very long time. 

#7 Stable Wormhole

Stable Wormhole is the first of a few great landfall cards on this list. This three-mana green enchantment makes a tapped planet land token every time you attack. It's simple, but it's going to give you an extra mana every single turn while triggering plenty of amazing cards, and it even effectively pays for itself in just three turns as well. 

#6 Will Riker, First in the Field

Will Riker, First in the Field is a four-mana red 4/3 that has a lot of potential. At the beginning of your combat step, it fetches up the two two land cards from your library and lets you put them into play. You have to sacrifice them in your end step, but if you can play them later using a different card, or you want to be sacrificing lands anyway, then it's an amazing card. That's to say nothing of how good it is in landfall decks. 

#5 Anthropological Mission

Anthropological Mission is a three-mana blue enchantment that lets you draw a card when you cast a noncreature spell, and then discard a card. Once you've done that three times you no longer have to discard. It's a really good uncommon, and with a lot of decks being focused on noncreature spells it's very well-positioned. 

#4 Genesis Device

Genesis Device is an absurdly good card. This three-mana green artifact lets you find a land or planet card as it enters and put it into play tapped. On top of that, you can pay five-mana and sacrifice it to also sacrifice any number of lands and put that many lands into play from your library tapped. It's Scapeshift with the added bonus of fetching up a land to begin with. Any landfall deck wants this immediately. 

#3 Federation Resupply 

Federation Resupply is a two-mana white sorcery that lets you fetch up an aura, equipment, or spacecraft from your deck and put it into your hand. You can also cast it from your graveyard for four mana using beam me up, as long as you return a creature you control to your hand at the same time. Tutors are always very strong, and Resupply has the added benefits of being flexible and optionally activating a second time.

#2 The Naked Time

The Naked Time is selling well because of George Takei's abs. It's a two-mana red saga that lets you fetch up a mountain initially, which is incredibly good in red, then lets you buff your creatures, then makes you sacrifice a land. It's a solid all-rounder with plenty of applications in not only Commander, but also any format where more mana is good…yes that's all of them. 

#1 Talisman of Indulgence

Talisman of Indulgence is our big winner this week. This two-mana artifact can tap for colorless, or red or black at the cost of one life. It's a great card in Commander, and this one is especially cool because it has Kefka on it showing off his fancy new earrings. We see these jump up every so often as players start buying up extras for new commander decks.

item.title: The 10 Cards Everybody Wants From Yu-Gi-Oh's Magnificent Maestros
item.description:
Yu-Gi-Oh!|finance

The 10 Cards Everybody Wants From Yu-Gi-Oh's Magnificent Maestros

Toon in for some competitive bangers, stay for the Grand Master Rares.

By Zachariah Butler

|

Published Nov 13, 2026

|

5 min read

Copy Link
TCGplayer Series: The Cards Everybody Wants

Magnificent Maestros has finally arrived, and with it comes the all-new Toon support that will shake up the meta like no other. We also get some incredible support for fan-favorites like Unchained and my personal favorite… Blue-Eyes!

The Cards Everybody Wants From Magnificent Maestros

With new Grandmaster Rares, just like the previously released Magnificent Monsters, it'll be quite interesting to see the titanic prices commanded once again. Let's see the main cards everyone is looking for though, starting with an obvious one.

#10 Mind Scan

Easily one of the most game-warping cards we've ever had, Mind Scan is just silly. For Duel Links players, the hand reveal technology is nothing new. We saw tons of cards forbidden that did that exact thing, preventing key cards from activating their effect. Vanquish Soul, Branded in High Spirits and even cards like the entire Blitzclique deck are just useless because you can't reveal something already being revealed. Mind Scan is also great at flooding out opposing power cards, so be on the watch out for that too!

#9 Rokket Barrage

Talk about a banger of a card! Rokket Barrage is perfect for the renewed Dragon Link strategy. Pitching a Dark Dragon to the grave to Special Summon Barrage would already be good, as we saw with cards like Noctovision Dragon years ago. However, it's that second effect that makes me raise an eyebrow. When it's targeted by a link monster, you can destroy your Barrage and Special Summon up to one "Rokket" monster each from your hand, Deck, graveyard and banishment, except "Rokket Barrage". Yeah, four free summons, that's what this card offers.

#8 Triple Borrel Launch

Another incredible extender for Dragon Link. This time, it also recycles resources. If you shuffle back one monster, you can Special Summon a different named Rokket from your deck. If you shuffle back two? Then you can add a Field Spell from your grave to your hand. If you shuffle back three, you can disrupt your opponent's grave! It's a neat card, and while I'm not completely sure how much table time it will get, it has some nice niche uses.

#7 Dark Rebellion Xyz Dragon, Four Heavenly Dragons



Phantom Knight was already a decent deck, having just won the Dutch Open Regional Qualfier, but now it's even better! On Summon, destroying tons of cards is obviously good. However, it gets even better when your opponent does anything. You get to summon a Rank 4 Xyz using your Dark Rebellion Xyz Dragon, Four Heavenly Dragons as material, which is obviously good. We've seen how good rank ups can be, and now Phantom Knights gets another!

#6 Blue-Eyes Ultimate Toon Dragon

Pegasus would be so proud! Blue-Eyes Ultimate Dragon looks significantly cuddlier now. Unlike many old fusions, this can be summoned by shuffling back materials from your hand, field or grave so that's good for your grind game. Then every turn you can add a Toon card or a card that specifically mentions a Toon monster by name to your hand. And if that wasn't enough, it's able to protect your other Toons by banishing them when they're attacked. Literal anime moment right there!

#5 Animimicat

An absolutely stellar starter card, Animimicat is a Lonefire Blossom for Toons, tributing itself to summon any Toon from your deck for free. However, if you're in control of a Toon World, you can tribute your opponent's monster instead! It's a Level 1 Beast-type monster too, so there's going to be some crazy synergy with the Tri-Brigade cards from that alone! This is an auto include in any Toon deck at a full three copies I'm sure, and it's easy to see why.

#4 Deep-Eyes White Dragon, the Blue Abyss



Oh boy, now we're talking. I've been waiting for months to talk about the new Blue-Eyes cards and anyone who has had to listen to me can attest to that. Deep-Eyes White Dragon, the Blue Abyss is a fantastic consistency tool. Adding a Level 1 Light Tuner, like Sage with Eyes of Blue? Yes please! It's also good at fetching cards like Effect Veiler, conveniently enough. For a more pure Blue-Eyes strategy, this is also great for recycling your Ritual Monsters, which are used for summon powerful boss monsters like Dragon Master Magia. This is an easy slot in for any Blue-Eyes deck.

#3 Blue-Eyes White Dragon, the Phantom Beast



Okay but this is the card I cannot shut up about! It's Snake-Eyes Poplar, but for Blue-Eyes! If it's added to your hand you can just slam it down, but that's not all. If it's summoned you can destroy every monster your opponent has, but you can only attack directly with Blue-Eyes monsters that turn.

Oh darn.

It's also protection from targeting, by discarding cards! It does everything!

#2 Funny Dark Rabbit



Another exceptionally good starter card, Funny Dark Rabbit provides additional summons and access to your key cards. Toon World can just be placed on the field, or Toon Kingdom for free! Bypassing the downsides of your main cards is always going to be good, and being treated as a Toon monster is also a boon when they have so many protective effects.

#1 Perfect Toon World

Instead of Toon Kingdom, you're likely going to play Perfect Toon World! Adding Toon cards or cards that mention them by name is going to be great, since you're deck thinning like a monster. Then, much like in the anime, you can dodge all sorts of silly effects with your Toon World spell by banishing monster effects. Perfect Toon World is the epitome of anime effects embodied, with all of the zany antics we saw Pegasus pull with his toon terrors.

Speaking of terrors, there were so many cards I didn't include and I'm sorry for that! The Unchained deck gets a ton of amazing support, propelling it to a potentially tier one spot. Cyber Dragons get a ton of really cool support cards as well! Even Blitzclique and Sacred Beasts get something thanks to Lightning Crash, now making Thunder decks more consistent than ever before. Magnificent Maestros has so much to offer, what are you excited for?

item.title: The 10 Chase Cards Everybody Wants from Mastery Pack: Assassin
item.description:
Flesh and Blood|collecting|finance

The 10 Chase Cards Everybody Wants from Mastery Pack: Assassin

Don't let powerful cards sneak up on you! Flesh and Blood's latest Mastery Pack is stuffed with must-have cards.

By Scott Mines

|@HowlingMines
|

Published Nov 13, 2026

|

8 min read

Copy Link
TCGplayer Series: The Cards Everybody Wants

Guys, gals and non-binary pals: the doctor is in.  

Even better, he's not the only one. Mastery Pack: Assassin is the latest instalment of Flesh and Blood's increasingly popular ancillary booster sets, designed to provide everything that fans of the Assassin class will need to get into the class, upgrade their decks and inflict crippling diseases on their opponent. 

It might just be the most important Mastery Pack so far. Mastery Pack: Assassin not only revitalizes neglected heroes like Uzuri, Switchblade and Arakni, Huntsman, but introduces the horrific Dr.Mortimer, Blight of the Pits into the Classic Constructed format. It's also the foundation for Outbreak, the first booster set of 2027. That's some awfully big boots to fill...

...and don't worry. I'll have an Armory Deck upgrade guide for Dr. Mortimer, Blight of the Pits for you next week. I'm in the kitchen myself, hang tight for a minute.

Somehow, Mastery Pack: Assassin has a little something for everyone despite clearly being tailored towards fans of the stabby stabby. If you're already deeply intrenched in the class, you're obviously covered — but there's also timely reprints for players entering the class for the first time and a handful of generics that'll fit into any collection. That's to say nothing of the high-end marvel collectibles. There's something for everyone in here!

So, what should you be hoping to find when you pop open those packs in the coming days? I'm glad you asked, mysterious voice on the internet. Here's some of my top picks for the most coveted cards from Flesh and Blood's Mastery Pack: Assassin. 

#10: Outbreak

You are not high enough on this card. There. I said it.  

Outbreak is the kind of card that's obviously powerful, but it's difficult to grasp how ubiquitous it has the potential to be until you've got a couple of games in. It's the golden rule in Flesh and Blood: "Blue block-threes that you actually want to play sometimes are kind of busted"

I think Outbreak is clearly at its best in Dr Mortimer, who can cure one of the ineffectual diseases to generate Silver, but a reaction that'll be worth upwards of five points of value that's so easily pitch stacked is appealing to any assassin. Taking all the tempo from your opponent with on-hits also lends itself towards cards that allow you to convert your full hand, which is exactly what Outbreak will allow you to do. 

#9: Banger!

You can't call a card Banger! and not design it as a certified banger.  

This card is horrific in the endgame when life totals begin to plummet, but it's also potentially quite strong as a blue that Uzuri, Switchblade is interested in switching in. If the opponent underblocks? Great, you're hitting for seven. If they overblock? Just leave your small attack on the chain and cash Banger! in for a Silver.

I'm also in love with the idea of pitch stacking a copy of this card next to a couple of Just a Nick, or sleeving it up in Kayo, Underhanded Cheat as a sweet target for your hero ability. It's so difficult to end up with a positive exchange for the opponent regardless of if they block or not.

I'm expecting Banger! to be a solid role player in several decks, so I'd suggest snapping up some copies while you can.  

#8: Remember the Mists

I feel similar ways about Remember the Mists as I do about Outbreak. While it's clearly at its best in a particular assassin, it's probably good enough to see universal play as a flexible blue with upside.  

Remember the Mists is Surgical Extraction at home. While you can't always rip away a meaningful card from the opposing hand, you can seriously mess with arrows and blue cards that the opponent intended to pitch away to fuel their turn. If you're really lucky, you'll find a pesky fabled gem in their hand and send it into the abyss forever.  

Despite the obvious power in Uzuri, I think Remember the Mists is also a meaningful upgrade to Arakni, Huntsman. The deck typically relies on Surgical Extraction to remove the final cards from the hand of an opponent that you're trying to fatigue. Remember the Mists provides another three blues that achieve the same thing, which is a pretty big boon in my book.  

#7: Expense Not Spared 

This card reads like Swordmaster's Shine just chugged an energy drink, but I actually think it's entirely fine at time of writing. Silver is a finite resource for many of these heroes and should be seen as a real cost to play Expense Not Spared.

Think about it this way: the floor for two silver is rebuying a Graven Gloves (or similar piece in a different slot), so we should consider two Silver to be worth at least two value. If you squint, that makes Expense Not Spared more of a +3 than a +5. That's still quite good, but it makes those comparisons to other cards a little misleading.  

The power of this card will come in forcing through on-hits. The best possible fork is having Dr.Mortimer, Blight of the Pits active as you attack to convince your opponent that you're looking for Go Again, then whacking them over the head with five damage at reaction speed instead.

#6: Important Assassin Reprints

I'm going to cobble a few of these together into one entry, so they don't eat up my entire list. The fact I need to consider doing that is a good sign for the health of Mastery Pack: Assassin.   

It's no secret that several of the staple assassin threats were getting a little expensive as the hype for Mastery Pack: Assassin and Outbreak began to swell. While this product didn't quite manage to tackle all those price increases (it was never going to), it does contain many important ones for players getting into Assassin.  

Persuasive Prognosis, Pain in the Backside and Blacktek Whisperers are staples of the class and should be cheaper than they have been in a long time in the immediate wake of release. There's no better time to purchase them if you've been sitting on your hands. 

#5: Phial of Calamity

It takes a really potent piece of kit to usurp a dagger, but I think Phial of Calamity has such a terrifying threat of activation is specific matchups that the juice will be worth the squeeze.  

In aggressive matchups where the opponent doesn't want to block, this says "if you ignore my dagger, your arsenal is gone". In Assassin/Ranger matchups, on-demand Frailty is both your best friend and fuels half the cost to get Phail of Calamity back into play. It also causes headaches once your opponent is sitting at three life because of Bloodrot Pox.  

In Arakni, 5L!p3d 7hRu 73h cR4X, I think this card is kind of heinous. Kiss of Death gets to double dip on whatever affliction you decided to afflict thanks to Flick Knives.  If you do that multiple times in a game? Disgusting. 

#4: Silver (Marvel)

Despite being the least flashy card on this list, the marvel variant of the Silver token is very flashy in real life. That's exactly why everybody is going to want it.  

Silver is slowly becoming an important part of every assassin's toolkit, and most Flesh and Blood players are magpies. If my deck makes Silver, I need the nice one or I'm a disgrace to my class. It really is as simple as that.  

#3: Cadaver Handlers

I'm down for you to quote me on this one. Cadaver Handlers are not only the best card in Mastery Pack: Assassin: they're one of the top five equipment ever printed.  

This thing is NUTS. It's never been more difficult to block a Codex of Frailty into a Leave No Witnesses. Cadaver Handlers effects the whole chain link for some reason, so even if you hold your defense reaction until after it's been activated, it'll still get shrunk.

Thankfully, that does mean that it won't break Temper equipment that hadn't blocked before, but that seems like a small reprieve. I bought a cold foil yesterday because I believe this card is stupid. I really can't think a better endorsement than that.  

#2: Dr. Mortimer, Blight of the Pits (Marvel)

In the era of FaB 3.0, I get the feeling that adult hero marvels are going to become a hot commodity. Frankly, they already were. Have you seen the price on Viserai, the Forsaken lately?!  

The vibe on Dr.Mortimer, Blight of the Pits heading into release is pretty darn good. There are high expectations for the hero straight out of the gate and an army of fans who love the Assassin class. I'm expecting the premium version of his adult hero card to become a small goldmine if he lives up to his potential.  

It shouldn't hit the highs of the Jarl Vetreidi marvel, but frankly it doesn't need to. 

#1: Dynasty Attack Marvels

But these might. What an absurd introduction to FAB 3.0!

Leave No Witnesses and Surgical Extraction have been a core part of Assassin's identity since the class first released back in Dynasty, while Eradicate has seen a strong amount of play for the weakest card in the cycle. This trio is assassin. It makes so much sense to give them the premium treatment as the headliner for this set. 

These are all going to be grails for collectors and players alike, but I'm expecting Leave No Witnesses to be in a league of its own. It's been a three of in every Assassin deck since it was printed, so those serious assassin players are going to see it as an incredibly worthwhile investment. 

Written By

Scott Mines

item.title: Boldly going where no Magic set has gone before.The 10 Cards Everybody Wants From Star Trekby Emma Merriam-PartlowRead More
item.description:
Magic: The Gathering|collecting|finance

The 10 Chase Cards Everybody Wants From Magic: The Gathering | Star Trek

Boldly going where no Magic set has gone before.

By Emma Merriam-Partlow

|

Published Nov 7, 2026

|

9 min read

Copy Link
TCGplayer Series: The Cards Everybody Wants

Magic: The Gathering | Star Trek is almost here! As the year draws to a close, Star Trek's the last release of the year and it introduces a new way to start your space-faring journey into Magic!

Releasing globally on November 13, Star Trek is the latest Universes Beyond release catered towards getting people into Magic. While it won't be as massive as FINAL FANTASY or The Lord of the Rings: Tales of Middle-earth, there's a deep appreciation for Star Trek, which is reflected in many of the card designs contained within the set. 

The 10 Chase Cards Everybody Wants From Magic: The Gathering | Star Trek

Today, I'll be guiding you through the cards you'll be keen to open in Play and Collector Boosters. While Star Trek won't be for everyone after the excitement of Reality Fracture, it's perhaps one of the more interestingly-designed Magic sets in a minute. If you're someone who's a little more entrenched yet can see past the Universes Beyond appeal, there's some genuinely good cards that will make an impact casually and perhaps even competitively. 

#10 Death is Irrelevant (LCARS Showcase)

"Death Is Irrelevant" is something I've probably said in a game of Commander or two at some point, but the Star Trek card packs a devastating punch if you love playing with artifacts. The card showcases what the Borg does best, recycling dead or near-dead creatures to expand The Collective. The Borg play a massive role in the Star Trek set, with the hive mind having their own dedicated Commander Deck and even Limited archetype for you to enjoy during Prerelease and beyond.

While eight mana is a lot to consider, Death Is Irrelevant makes your artifact creatures indestructible while assimilating a creature from any graveyard during your endstep to expand The Collective. Assimilate is a new mechanic introduced in Star Trek, which turns a creature into an Borg artifact creature along with getting a +1/+1 counter to boot. With the enchantment, it means you can slowly turn the tide of battle and embrace every creature to become one with the Borg, something that is rather on-theme and will lead you to a convincing victory. 

#9 Starbase Yorktown (Talon Gates of Madara)

There's a lot going on with Star Trek which may make it tricky to understand the release if you're new to Magic, but the Stardates cards are a series of reprints reimagined with Star Trek flavor. There's 30 of these to collect and showcase popular characters and moments from the Star Trek franchise, this includes the movies in addition to the television series. As for the cards themselves, many of the reprints are quite playable if you're someone more entrenched into Magic who can move past the visual aesthetic. In particular, Starbase Yorktown is a reprint of Talon Gates of Madara, one of the best utility lands printed for Commander play as of late. This one debuted in Commander: Modern Horizons 3 several years ago, and it's slowly risen in price as it provides decent protection for your commander (or biggest threat) from opposing removal or effects. 

Sure, it might be challenging to acknowledge Benedict Cumberbatch as a Phyrexian Praetor, but there's some serious reprint value in the Stardates cards that could offer an affordable opportunity to buy a couple down the line. That said, these are ideal if you're someone who adores the Star Trek franchise and want to collect some of your favorite characters in cardboard form. 

#8 Lwaxana Troi, Charming Guest (Extended Art)

Roaming Throne remains a menace at the Commander tables, and despite my strong feelings about the card, Lwaxana Troi, Charming Guest provides the effect in a more interesting way for multiplayer. Lwaxana Troi provides an extra ability trigger for a selected creature for as long as she's tapped, and you can choose to leave her tapped during your untap step. As someone who's unfamiliar with Star Trek but has been checking out the lore, this is a really flavorful way to design the ambassador. 

Given her larger-than-life and flirtatious nature, Lwaxana Troi will be an exciting card to play at the casual tables. The fact you have to consider which creature to grant the "triggers an additional time" ability creates an interesting mini-game, more than Roaming Throne ever could offer. While normal copies of Lwaxana Troi won't be too hard to find, extended art copies are exclusive to Collector Boosters and will be the premier version to own if you're someone who likes the fanciest versions to play with. 

#7 U.S.S. Enterprise-D, Galaxy-Class (Extended Art)

Unsurprising to literally anyone, Spacecraft and the station make a notable return in Star Trek. Debuting in Edge of Eternities last year, Spacecraft has become a curious way to design artifacts that permanently become creatures once stationed with enough power. One of the many Spacecraft cards appearing in Star Trek is U.S.S. Enterprise-D, Galaxy-Class, which happens to be the ship under the command of Captain Jean-Luc Picard. 

Legendary tenure in media aside, the Magic card looks flavorful yet exciting for casual play. What strikes me the most is the ability to exile a card from the top of your library whenever you add a charge counter to U.S.S. Enterprise-D, and you're able to play that card on that turn. Essentially, this gives the Enterprise an Impulse-like effect — as if the spaceship has impulse engines or something. One thing to keep in mind with Universes Beyond is there will always be a desire to own cards of popular characters, moments or otherwise that may not even be played. U.S.S. Enterprise-D, Galaxy-Class is certainly one of them.

#6 Genesis Device (Classic Enterprise Showcase)

What if you could Scapeshift, but do so with a permanent instead? 


That's what Genesis Device is looking to do, providing an incredible way to trigger multiple instances of landfall and even fill up the graveyard for Crucible of Worlds-like effects. This is a must-have for Toph, the First Metalbender if you're someone who loves Avatar: The Last Airbender, as she's able to earthbend the artifact and it'll come back to play once sacrificed to the activated ability. It's also quite good with Shifting Woodland, and for as long as you have delirium, you can sacrifice the Device and make a copy of it from the graveyard and spin the wheel once more!

This is probably my sleeper card from the set, Scapeshift has become rather expensive due to the popularity of Land-matter archetypes led by Lord Windgrace, Tifa Lockhart, and Hearthhull, the Worldseed in Commander, so having access to more affordable options is ideal. Bearing in mind that Genesis Device is an artifact, allowing you to search for it with Fabricate or similar. Not to mention, it's a three-mana Rampant Growth which is just icing on the cake!

#5 Quark, Humble Proprietor (Borderless Scene)

Treasure tokens remain emblematic to Commander's identity, allowing a one-time ramp without much effort. While The Hobbit brought us Smaug the Magnificent as a reward for having a pile of Treasure tokens under your control, Quark, Humble Proprietor offers an incredible way to start amassing it. During each player's upkeep, you'll create a Treasure token with Quark in play, however, you won't be able to sacrifice those tokens for mana. While this is a hefty downside for the amount of Treasures you'll have in an average game of Commander, it's easy enough to remove Quark from play and be on your way. 

Star Trek is riddled with unique designs we haven't seen elsewhere in Magic, and I suspect Quark will be a desirable card to own due to how much Treasure tokens appear in Commander these days. Even if you aren't someone who's familiar with the source material, the design is interesting enough that it'll be worth something in the months to come. As with any Universes Beyond release these days, borderless scene cards make a return in Star Trek with Quark, Humble Proprietor being one of many to collect. 

#4 Deep Space 9 (Extended Art)

Sentiments I mentioned with the U.S.S. Enterprise-D, Galaxy-Class also apply to Deep Space 9, an iconic space station with many Star Trek fans wanting to own the card from the set. The card happens to be rather strong also, as you're able to exile the top four cards of your library and put all permanent cards exiled this way onto the battlefield during your upkeep. This even accounts for lands, meaning you have a fairly consistent way of ramping if you really need it. However, the real reason to play the card is to develop a battlefield filled to the brim with variants of the Enterprise while offering a potent boost to all of your creatures if you station it. To me, this looks like the best Spacecraft in Star Trek, and one that'll devastate Commander tables upon release.

#3 Dr. Beverly Crusher (LCARS Showcase, Surge Foil)

If there's one thing casual Commander players love having are cards that can double-up on triggered or activated abilities. Dr. Beverly Crusher causes a triggered ability of a permanent you control to trigger again if you've gained life, which also extends to Crusher herself as she's essentially a super-charged Ajani's Pridemate. 

With Reality Fracture's Kwia Vigorbloom remaining a popular option to play in Commander, having cards like Dr. Beverly Crusher enables you to reap more out of the various Soul Warden triggers while also developing the battlefield in several other ways. Lifegain continues to be a desirable way to play Commander, and I suspect opening any copy of Dr. Beverly Crusher will bring modest value along with strong player demand. In particular, the LCARS surge foil printing will be the most expensive one you can open from the set, and is exclusive to Collector Boosters. 

#2 The Shock Lands (LCARS Showcase, Surge Foil)

Even if you're someone who isn't as familiar with Star Trek, you have to admit the latest reprints of the Shock Lands are much-needed. Shock Lands remain some of the best mana options ever printed in Magic, yet have an extensive history both casually and competitively. With Star Trek, all ten Shock Lands see a reprint with a chance of opening the gorgeous LCARS treatments on release day and beyond. These appear in both Play and Collector Boosters, with surge foil copies exclusive to Collector Boosters. Opening any Shock Land will be useful to either play with or trade towards something you're actually after, but the greatest value will be in the surge foil copies as these appear less than 5% of the time in Collector Boosters. 

#1 The Autographed Star Trek Actor Cards

Star Trek takes us to a strange new world of collectibility, as the set introduces autographed cards for the very first time. There's seven of these stunning cards to collect and appear in extremely low quantities in Collector Boosters, with the cards being:

  • Captain Kathryn Janeway
  • Captain James T. Kirk
  • Lt. Cmdr. Geordi La Forge
  • Mr. Spock, Science Officer
  • Seven of Nine, Unassimilated
  • Lieutenant Commander Data
  • Captain Jean-Luc Picard

The actors of Star Trek continue to be ubiquitous with the franchise even today, meaning this collection will be the cards everyone will want to open from the Universes Beyond release. There are fewer than 250 copies of each card in existence, which suggests the secondary market value for these cards will be desirable enough with Star Trek collectors and players. While none of the autographed cards have made their way to TCGplayer or eBay quite yet, an autographed Captain Kathryn Janeway has already been opened in the lead up to the set's release next week.
